items.title: Reconvene to Open Session / Report Out on Closed Session

publicComments.name: Aida Vasquez
publicComments.summary: Spoke in Spanish as a Garfield School parent opposing proposed changes to the bilingual program, expressing that bilingual classes have been effective and asking the board to support and maintain rather than change the existing program.

publicComments.name: Michelle Strode
publicComments.summary: Spoke as an Orion School TK and kindergarten parent requesting expansion of after-school programs at Orion to support working families who cannot fully utilize the TK program without reliable after-school care.

publicComments.name: Sally Dunaway Young
publicComments.summary: Spoke as an Orion parent urging the board to allocate additional campus space to qualified aftercare providers so they can expand to meet demand from working families with TK students.

publicComments.name: Mei Liang
publicComments.summary: Spoke as an incoming Orion kindergarten parent from San Carlos advocating for the addition of a third Play Thrive classroom to support families waitlisted for after-school care in the Mandarin immersion program.

publicComments.name: Catherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Spoke as a parent of a former Mandarin immersion student now at North Star, thanking Dr. Baker for his years of support for both the Mandarin immersion and North Star programs.

publicComments.name: Josh Hill
publicComments.summary: Echoed other parents' comments welcoming his child's acceptance to the Orion Mandarin program and requesting expansion of after-school care to alleviate anxiety about placement.

publicComments.name: Lilia Amalia Valdez-Monet
publicComments.summary: Spoke as a longtime Hoover community volunteer and parent advocate urging the board to support smaller class sizes and additional assistance, noting that one Spanish kindergarten class with many high-need students is insufficient for equitable education.

publicComments.name: Sophia Santos
publicComments.summary: Spoke as a first-grade teacher at Hoover School urging the board to prioritize manageable class sizes, citing research supporting smaller classes in primary grades and describing her own class of 27 students with high percentages of IEP, multilingual learner, and behavioral needs.

publicComments.name: Christy Herrera
publicComments.summary: Spoke as a Hoover kindergarten teacher with deep roots in RCSD as a former student, parent, and 34-year combined community member, urging the board to invest in smaller class sizes and equitable support, describing her current class of 28 students with high IEP, multilingual, and behavioral needs.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: Spoke as CSEA Chapter 5 President expressing eagerness to hear the Roy Cloud and Clifford school reports and the CTA presentation.
